Title: ICQA Data Analyst
Description:
Description

At Amazon, we're working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people. If you'd like to help us build the place to find and buy anything online, this is your chance to make history.

Amazon Canada Fulfillment Services is hiring a Data Analyst to support the Inventory Control / Quality Assurance (ICQA) team. The Data Analyst assigned to ICQA will work closely with the ICQA and operations teams in Inbound and Outbound to provide data and analytical support for ACES initiatives, root cause investigation of defects, and will provide support to ensure compliance to ICQA-related SoX requirements.

The Data Analyst will own the insights, set up analysis, and create automated dashboards and reporting. They will be responsible for identifying data sources (internal / external) to invent and simplify mechanisms and create custom reporting and analytics automation tools.

Operating in a fast-moving and sometimes ambiguous environment, you will be required to work autonomously, taking full control and responsibility for achieving business objectives. This role provides real opportunity to develop original ideas, approaches and solutions in an ever-changing and competitive business climate.

Key job responsibilities


Development of data collection processes and data management systems
Maintenance of data integrity (0% error rate)
Designing of queries, compiling of data, and generation of reports in MS Excel
Charting and graphing of data for reporting purposes
In depth research of defect trends
Data collection and entry as needed
Data mining and problem solving
Back up for Process Assistant duties


Basic Qualifications


2+ years of professional or military experience
Work 40 hours/week, and overtime as required
Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
Are 18 years of age or older
2+ years of business analyst, data analyst or an equivalent role experience
1+ years of using SQL to extract and manipulate data experience
Bachelor's degree, or High school or equivalent diploma
2+ years of professional work experience, or experience in MS Office, with an emphasis on Excel
Experience writing complex Excel VBA macros
Experience in advanced SQL, Python, Tableau
Experience demonstrating problem solving and root cause analysis
Experience with modern software development, web development frameworks, APIs
1+ years of project management experience


Preferred Qualifications


3+ years of business analyst, data analyst or similar role experience
Experience in written and verbal communication skills to communicate with technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership
Experience dealing well with ambiguity, prioritizing needs, and delivering measurable results in an agile environment
Experience programming with at least one software programming language, or experience with full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations
Knowledge of data warehousing and data modeling
Experience with data scripting languages (e.g., SQL, Python, R, or equivalent) or statistical/mathematical software (e.g., R, SAS, Matlab, or equivalent)
Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Statistics, Computer Science, Mathematics, Supply Chain or related field.

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. Title: Senior Operations Data Analyst (Hybrid)
Description:
Your opportunity

By joining the Kardium team, you can help make a difference in the lives of millions around the world. We have developed a ground-breaking medical device for the diagnosis and treatment of the most common heart rhythm disorder, atrial fibrillation – which can cause stroke, heart failure, and other heart-related complications.

Kardium’s mission is to deliver the best treatment for atrial fibrillation. To achieve this, we have developed The Globe® Pulsed Field System – we have a fantastic technical team that has developed a product with strong, unique, and customer-valued differentiators versus other solutions on the market. We have built connections with key opinion leaders who are already using the Globe System and are helping to tell our story.

We have obtained FDA approval and officially begun the commercial launch of the Globe® Pulsed Field System. This is a pivotal and exciting time in our journey, as we bring this life-changing technology to patients!

We are seeking an Operational Analyst who you will be responsible for delivering high-impact dashboards, metrics and reporting across various operational teams. You will play a critical role in enabling real-time operational visibility and data-informed decision-making, supporting both daily execution and strategic planning initiatives. The analyst will work cross-functionally with operations, purchasing, and quality teams, with a strong focus on data quality and continuity during our transition to Microsoft Dynamics 365 ERP system.

Please note, this opportunity is a hybrid work arrangement, located in Burnaby, BC.

Meaningful work you will be a part of

Your Responsibilities Will Include


Develop and maintain critical operational metrics and key process indicators (KPIs) to support manufacturing, planning, and quality functions
Create and manage visual dashboards to provide real time insight into operational performance using tools such as Power BI and Excel
Provide analytical support for continuous improvement initiatives and projects to identify and prioritize optimization opportunities for cost reduction and performance improvements.
Query and extract relevant data from ERP and other data sources using SQL or other relevant tools.
Partner with cross-functional teams to identify data requirements and alignment with operational goals
Collaborate with stakeholders to develop scalable reporting frameworks and templates to support future growth.
Advise on data architecture and structure as systems evolve and new systems introduced, ensuring the right data is collected and accessible.
Lead initiatives to improve data quality and governance, identifying gaps and implementing data validation processes.
Train and support end-users in interpreting dashboard data and utilizing insights for decision-making.
Ensure data security and compliance with relevant regulations and company policies.


What You Bring To The Team

Our Kardium team is smart, creative, and passionate about developing cutting-edge medical devices to help improve people’s lives. We work in a collaborative environment based on trust and respect. We understand that only by working together can we solve what was thought unsolvable.

You will be successful in this role because you possess these attributes:


Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business Analytics, Information Systems, or a related field.
Minimum 5 years experience in data analytics or reporting in a manufacturing or supply chain environment.
Advanced skills in Power BI, SQL and Excel.
Highly analytic and data driven with the ability to organize data and derive conclusions
Demonstrated experience building and maintaining dashboards and reporting systems used by cross-functional teams.
Strong understanding of operational process (manufacturing, supply chain) as well as key operations metrics (e.g., OEE, throughput, inventory turns, supplier performance).
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
Experience working with ERP systems (Microsoft D365 or equivalent is a strong asset).
Knowledge and experience working in the regulated manufacturing industry is an asset.


Compensation

Kardium has listed the total cash compensation range (base salary + 5% RRSP contribution) that we expect to pay applicants for this role, as of the time of this posting. Pay offered will be determined based on numerous relevant business and candidate factors including, for example, education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, and business or organizational needs. For candidates with more or less experience than listed above, the pay range will be adjusted.

As a permanent employee, you will also participate in Kardium’s stock option plan.


$90,000 – 125,000 (CAD Annually)


Your Benefits & Well-being

The total cash we’ve listed for this position includes a base salary, plus an annual contribution to a Retirement Savings Plan account to help support your financial goals.

Comprehensive medical & dental coverage for all permanent employees – effective as of Day 1, with no waiting period.

Work-day flexibility – we offer a flexible work environment for daily working hours. In addition, we provide 3 personal days per year.

Support for you (and your dependents) overall well-being.

Family building – we provide top up for maternity leave, adoptive leave, and parental leave for non-birthing parents. Employees can also enroll in benefit coverage for fertility drug treatment.

Career progression and learning support.

Professional membership support.

Life at Kardium

What makes us a great place to work?


Our Purpose
Our People
Our Culture


At Kardium, we embrace diversity of background, experience, and perspective and we’re committed to inclusion and equity at every level. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates who represent the full diversity of all communities.

We collaborate with Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), as volunteer-led groups who share a common dimension of diversity and come together to provide support, education, and other opportunities across Kardium. Examples of our ERGs include Women ERG, Pride ERG, Race Ethnicity & Cultural Heritage (REACH) ERG, Truth & Reconciliation ERG, Persian ERG, Chinese ERG, Barangay Kardium (Filipino) ERG, Irish ERG, Brazilian ERG, and Early Career at Kardium ERG.

Title: Data Analyst
Description:
Interested in joining one of Canada's top performing asset managers? We are looking for a Data Analyst to join our Enterprise Data Solutions team. In this role, you'll help build integrated, reliable, and scalable data solutions that support business decision-making across the organization. Working with enterprise platforms such as Salesforce, Greenhouse, and Dayforce, you'll collaborate with business and technology partners to analyze data, support system integrations, improve data quality, and contribute to impactful enterprise-wide data initiatives. If you're curious, analytical, and enjoy working at the intersection of business, data, and technology, this could be an exciting next step in your career. Our offices operate on a hybrid model with three days per week in-office to support team collaboration.

What You Will Do


Analyze and profile data across enterprise systems to identify trends, issues, and opportunities for improvement.
Partner with business and technology stakeholders to gather requirements and translate them into data solutions.
Support the design and development of scalable data models and data structures for reporting, analytics, and integrations.
Collaborate with data engineers and application teams to define and validate data transformation rules.
Test and validate REST APIs, integrations, and data flows between business applications and data platforms.
Perform data quality, reconciliation, and validation activities to ensure accuracy and completeness of information.
Develop and execute test cases for data mappings, APIs, and end-to-end integration processes.
Document data models, mappings, integration requirements, and technical processes.
Participate in Agile delivery activities, including testing, defect resolution, and release validation.
Help identify opportunities to improve data usability, consistency, and operational efficiency across the organization.


What You Bring


3-5 years of experience in data analysis, business systems analysis, data integration, or a related technology role.
Strong SQL skills with experience querying and analyzing relational data.
Experience working with enterprise applications such as Salesforce, Dayforce, Greenhouse, or similar CRM, ATS, HRIS, or SaaS platforms.
Knowledge of relational data modelling concepts and data integration principles.
Experience working with and testing REST APIs, including JSON and API testing tools such as Postman.
Strong experience in data validation, reconciliation, and data quality analysis.
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to document requirements, data mappings, testing activities, and technical processes.
Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work across technical and non-technical teams.
Familiarity with Agile delivery practices and software development lifecycles.
Experience with Power BI or other reporting and analytics platforms.
Experience with Python or another scripting language.
Exposure to cloud-based data platforms, data warehouses, or modern data technologies.
Experience working with HR, recruiting, CRM, finance, or other enterprise business data.
Financial services or other regulated industry experience.


The starting salary for this position is $110,000 - $130,000. The starting salary provided reflects the base salary for this position as required by legislation. In addition, there is an annual performance bonus which contributes to the total compensation of this position. Further questions may be directed to the HR team during the interview process.

For a closer look at how you can build your career with us, we invite you to explore cclgroup.com. 

CC&L Financial Group is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to gender, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation or expression, disability, or age. 

Your application will be reviewed by a member of the hiring team - AI is not used in the screening, assessment or selection of applications at this time.

Title: Data Analyst II, Fraud
Description:
Job Description:

At Remitly, we believe everyone deserves the freedom to access, move, and manage their money wherever life takes them. Since 2011, we've tirelessly delivered on our promise to customers sending money globally, providing secure, simple, and reliable ways to manage their money, ensuring true peace of mind.

Whether it's supporting loved ones back home, growing a business across continents, or pursuing new opportunities abroad, we're not just here to move money— we're here to move our global customers forward.

We're looking for builders, reimaginers, and global thinkers who want to work at the intersection of technology, trust, and transformation. If that's you and you're ready to do the most meaningful work of your career—we invite you to join over 2,800 passionate Remitlians worldwide who are united by our vision to transform lives with trusted financial services that transcend borders

About the Role:

As a Data Analyst, Fraud, you will be part of Remitly's Identity & Trust Analytics Team. Your mission is to leverage analytical methods to identify, prevent, and mitigate fraud impacting our customers globally. You will develop a deep understanding of Remitly's fraud detection systems, regional risk profiles, and operational processes to improve fraud defenses while maintaining a seamless experience for legitimate customers. You'll partner with Product, Engineering, Business Management, and Compliance to customize and optimize fraud models and workflows, integrating data from legacy and new platforms. This hybrid role requires 2–3 days per week in the Vancouver office.

You Will:


Become an expert on Remitly's fraud data (e.g. chargebacks, promo abuse, scams, onboarding risk).
Build data-driven models and dashboards to analyze and monitor fraud exposure, balancing customer experience with operational efficiency.
Collect, normalize, and analyze data from legacy prebriefs, transaction logs, and onboarding systems to identify fraud trends and behavior anomalies.
Partner with Business Management and Product to continuously improve customer verification, KYC, KYB and compliance workflows.
Design and evaluate experiments and A/B tests to measure fraud control effectiveness and minimize false positives.
Develop and track risk metrics that quantify fraud exposure, policy compliance, and system performance.
Provide actionable insights and influence the development of fraud detection strategies, tools, and automation.


You Have:


3+ years in an analytics or fraud/risk analysis role within fintech, e-commerce, or digital payments.
Experience with fraud or trust analytics.
Bachelor's degree in mathematics, engineering, economics, or another quantitative discipline (or equivalent experience).
Proficiency with SQL and hands-on experience analyzing large datasets (Python, R, or statistical modeling experience preferred).
Strong understanding of fraud taxonomies (chargebacks, identity theft, scams, onboarding risk, and promo abuse).
Demonstrated ability to distill business problems, develop hypotheses, perform analysis, and communicate clear recommendations.
Excellent data storytelling and communication skills; ability to translate complex findings into business decisions.


Compensation Details. The starting base salary range for this position is $100,000 - $125000. In Canada, Remitly employees are shareholders in our Company and equity is part of our total compensation plan. Your recruiter can share more information about medical benefits offered, as well as other financial benefits and total compensation components offered with this role.

Our Benefits


Four weeks vacation
Health Benefits
Mental Health & Family Forming Benefits
RRSP plan with company match
Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)
Life Insurance & Disability
Continuing education and travel benefits


Our Connected Work Culture: Driving Innovation, Together

At Remitly, we believe that true innovation sparks when we come together. Our Connected Work Culture fosters dynamic in-person collaboration, where ideas ignite and challenging problems find solutions faster.Under the Company's current hybrid-work expectations, employees in this position work onsite Tuesday through Thursday each week. Additional onsite attendance may be required based on business needs, and the Company may modify its hybrid-work expectations from time to time. These intentional in-office moments are vital for deepening relationships, fueling creativity, and ensuring your impact is felt where it matters most.

Remitly is an E-Verify Employer

At Remitly, we are dedicated to ensuring that our workplace offers equal employment opportunities to all employees and candidates, in full compliance with applicable laws and regulations.

Remitly is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Title: Quantitative Equity Data Analyst
Description:
We are looking for a Data Analyst to join our Quantitative Equity Team! We are a high-performance team embedded in a top-performing quantitative equity fund that manages over $78+ billion USD in financial assets. We are dedicated to the mission-critical operation of our investment engine—a well-tuned machine responsible for generating key decisions that drive trades and investment insights. Leveraging data analytics, finance knowledge and cutting-edge technology, we aim to ensure that new and useful data products are continuously ready for research.

Do you love the idea of integrating large proprietary data sources into valuable applications? Are you a wizard at transforming ‘messy reality’ into high quality data assets? As a core member of our team, you will collaborate with investment and data experts to tackle challenging problems, and to continuously expand our capabilities in data. Based on the west coast in Vancouver, we value mentorship, collaboration, and growth in a supportive and innovative environment. Join us to make a significant impact on our investment outcomes and overall success.

What You Will Do

This is an exciting full-time role for individuals who are enthusiastic about learning the quantitative equity investment management business and excited to tackle a broad range of data, investment, and technology challenges.

You will start with a comprehensive training program, learning about various elements of quantitative equity investment management and our investment process.

You will then continue to a specialized role utilizing data analytics and data science skillsets to enable the Quantitative Equity Team’s research. Your role will involve identifying and assessing brand new data, data exploration, and proposing robust ways to integrate data products from many sources.

You will be supported with coaching and mentorship from senior members of the team, and we will create the conditions for you to grow your career steadily over time. This is an opportunity for ambitious individuals

to drive their career growth in data.

Role

While we take the approach of tailoring the career path to individual strengths, we expect successful candidates for this role to develop excellence in the following tasks:


Create processes to assess, explore, and link billions of data points.
Test structured and unstructured data sets for data quality and reliability.
Assess new data opportunities for quality and usefulness.
Evaluate your data solutions for sensibility, accuracy, and bias.
Collaborate with quantitative researchers – support alpha projects with your data expertise.
Collaborate with technology specialists – help trade off application performance and operational feasibility.
Support production deployments of your work to ensure long-term reliability.
Enable clarity of and access to your work through robust documentation and exposition.
Present findings and recommendations to key stakeholders in a clear, concise, and compelling manner.


What You Bring


Analytical Mindset – You think critically and creatively and are adept at balancing intuition with statistical validation.
Financial Knowledge – Desire to acquire the financial context needed to understand your stakeholders and make data decisions with impact.
Self-Starter – You are motivated and willing to take personal accountability for quality and timeliness of work.
Collaborative Approach – You thrive in a collaborative environment and value shared success. You proactively solicit and provide input and excel at communicating complex and technical concepts.
Time Management – You are able to manage and prioritize multiple ongoing projects.
Academic Training – At a minimum, an undergraduate degree in finance, mathematics, statistics, computer science, engineering, or related discipline. Completion of a relevant graduate degree is considered an asset.


We welcome applications from candidates with different levels of experience, including interns, new graduates, and experienced professionals. The base salary range for full-time roles is $125,000 – $200,000 annually plus a competitive performance bonus. Compensation will be determined based on experience and qualifications.

To apply for this position, please submit your resume, cover letter and academic transcripts.

CC&L Financial Group is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to gender, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation or expression, disability, or age. 

Your application will be reviewed by a member of the hiring team - AI is not used in the screening, assessment or selection of applications at this time.

Title: Marketing, Data Analyst
Description:
Why BCAA?

Feel proud of what you do and help shape the future of BC at a BC Top Employer. We’re driven by purpose – delivering peace of mind to one in three BC households with insurance, roadside assistance, auto repair, Evo Car Share and Evolve E-Bike Share. With a long history of keeping roads safe and giving back in ways that build stronger communities, we offer a wide variety of meaningful, rewarding careers that move BC forward.

We are currently hiring a Marketing Data Analyst to join our Digital Engagement team based at our Head Office in Burnaby.

In this role, you will help build a data-driven, customer-obsessed culture by turning complex data into meaningful insights, improving campaign targeting and measurement, and supporting the tools and data that power BCAA’s marketing programs. You will work closely with Marketing, Information Services, Product Management and Customer Experience to develop dashboards, segmentation, automated customer journeys and predictive models that improve marketing performance and customer experiences.

Who you are:


You are a curious, critical thinker who enjoys exploring complex data and turning it into clear, actionable insights.
You are detail-oriented and quality-conscious, with a strong focus on accuracy, documentation and repeatable work.
You are a proactive problem-solver who can manage multiple priorities and move work forward independently.
You communicate technical information clearly and can translate between business stakeholders and technical teams.
You are collaborative and build strong relationships across functions.
You are passionate about using analytics, testing and technology to improve marketing performance and customer experiences.



What you’ll do:


Perform descriptive analysis by extracting, exploring and analyzing data from multiple sources, then develop summaries, visualizations and reports that provide useful business insights.
Create and maintain dashboards, define metrics with business partners, visualize key performance indicators and support data quality for effective decision-making.
Help develop BCAA’s marketing analytics strategy and support projects where marketing data and analytics enable or directly drive business outcomes.
Build campaign audiences and segmentation, develop SQL campaign queries, create campaign flow charts and support deployment lists.
Design and automate customer communication journeys using Salesforce Marketing Cloud Journey Builder and Automation Studio.
Develop and apply testing approaches for target groups, offers and creative, then translate results into recommendations that support a test-and-learn culture.
Build, implement and maintain predictive models to identify customer targets, next-best-product opportunities, multi-product purchasers and lifetime value.
Partner with cross-functional teams to improve data quality, enable commercial marketing and sales programs, and enhance customer experiences.
Work with Information Services and Data Engineering to improve the flow, accessibility and use of marketing data across Amazon Redshift, Salesforce Marketing Cloud and Financial Services Cloud.
Support website analytics and tracking strategy, and help implement Salesforce Marketing Cloud data enablement.
Streamline and automate analytics processes, writing high-quality code that is clear, documented and repeatable.
Follow privacy and customer contact standards for data use and file transfers, and document data sources, analyses and algorithms.



What you bring:


A post-secondary degree in data science, marketing analytics, commerce, statistics or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Approximately five years of relevant experience, including experience in marketing automation, business intelligence, customer insights or applied customer experience analytics.
Hands-on experience querying complex relational databases using SQL.
Experience creating dashboards and visualizations in Power BI or Tableau, and working with data in a Microsoft Fabric or comparable analytics environment.
Experience with Salesforce Marketing Cloud or another campaign management platform, including audience segmentation and customer journey orchestration.
Experience with Google Analytics and/or working knowledge of GA4.
Proficiency with statistical tools or languages such as R or Python, including experience with techniques such as regression, decision trees, segmentation, clustering or classification.
Experience managing large, complex or multi-source data sets with strong attention to quality and accuracy.
Knowledge of database modelling, data structures, data wrangling and data pipeline concepts such as APIs, ETL, FTP and workflow orchestration.
Strong project management, analytical, communication and interpersonal skills.
Experience with Amazon Redshift, Salesforce CRM, Financial Services Cloud, digital media metrics or audience management tools is an asset.
Experience in financial services is an asset.



The salary range for this position is $91,185.84 to $113,982.36 and is determined via job-related knowledge, skills, experience, certifications, market demand and internal equity. In addition to base salary and BCAA benefits, this position is eligible for a performance bonus target of 9%, with the opportunity to earn up to 15%.

What we offer:


The chance to make a difference every day in the lives of British Columbians, BCAA Members and our communities.
Career and personal development to help you grow and reach your goals.
Incentives that recognize team and individual sales and performance.
Flexible benefits to support your health and lifestyle, and wellness dollars* to keep your body, mind and soul thriving.
A competitive rewards package including salary performance bonus programs, pension plan*, and more to help build your personal wealth.
Paid time off including vacation, and days for wellness, volunteering, and cultural, spiritual or religious connection.
BCAA membership, with valuable perks and Member savings on every day and special spending, from gas and coffee to clothes, sports and event tickets, and hotels.
Meaningful, rewarding work for a BC Top Employer known for putting people first and constantly building a better workplace for all our team members.

Title: Data Analyst, Investment Data Management
Description:
Interested in joining one of Canada’s top performing asset managers? We are looking for a Data Analyst for an existing vacancy on our Investment Data Management (IDM) team. The IDM Team resides within the middle office and is responsible for managing data centric processes and data quality that supports the investment management business. Connor, Clark & Lunn Financial Group Ltd. (CCLFG) manages a wide range of global assets and heavily relies on the output of the Data Management Team for a variety of functions from the front office to the back. This is a fantastic opportunity to be part of a dynamic strategic team whose scope and importance continues to grow enterprise wide. We place a high value on maintaining an entrepreneurial spirit and creating a culture where each of us has opportunities to succeed. We are a solution orientated and collaborative team seeking like-minded individuals who thrive in a challenging and dynamic environment. Our offices currently operate on a hybrid model with a combination of in-office and remote working days throughout the week.

What You Will Do


Maintain and validate accuracy of equity/fixed income/derivative data across multiple systems/databases to enable Investment Manager modeling, trading, and risk monitoring.
Manage and enable a myriad of scheduled processes for vendor systems, internal and market data transfers, valuation, and benchmarking data inputs to the investment process.
Deliver timely data signoffs to investment teams; develop and analyze data-quality exceptions and ensure timely resolution.
Provide analysis on operational needs, ad-hoc data/data-history requests for multiple business partners to support pre- and post-trade portfolio management functions.
Identify process/workflow improvements to increase operational efficiency, mitigate risk, improve data-quality, and increase service levels provided to stakeholders.
Supporter of other operational or engineering staff, senior or managers on a variety of ad-hoc tasks and projects.


What You Bring


You have a degree in Finance, Commerce, Business Administration, Business Operations, or a related field. Relevant designation, such as the MBA, CFA, or FRM is an asset.
2-6 years of relevant experience in the investment management industry with exposure to securities data, data quality and process management. Hands-on experience working with Bloomberg, FTSE, ICE Bond Edge, Charles River and related financial tools, platforms is an asset
You possess an analytical mindset and able to break down complex processes into components to logically deduce the root cause of issues in data and technology.
You have a collaborative spirit that helps you to work well with others and you communicate effectively to team/cross-team members, and upward to key stakeholders.
You have a passion for advancing the quality, scale, and efficiency of data processes and can take ownership of multiple processes with keen attention to detail.
You constantly take a critical eye to processes with the goal of finding improvement opportunities and bring an ability to manage multiple projects.


The salary range for this position is $60,000-$90,000. The salary range provided reflects the base salary range for this position as required by legislation. In addition, there is an annual performance bonus which contributes to the total compensation for this position. Further questions may be directed to the HR team during the interview process.

Title: Data Analyst
Description:
Location: Vancouver / Toronto / Remote in Canada | Employment Type: Full-time |

Reports to: Senior Data Analyst, Team Lead

Reporting to Senior Data Analyst, Team Lead, we're looking for a curious and collaborative Data Analyst (Survey Tabulations) to join Reach3 Insights. In this role, you'll help turn survey data into accurate, decision-ready cross-tabulations, working with smart, kind people who love turning human insights into clear stories, stronger decisions, and better customer experiences.

This role is open to candidates based in Canada, with a remote working model designed to support connection, focused work, and real life outside of work.

About Reach3 Insights

Reach3 Insights is a full-service research consultancy that helps modern brands move faster and get closer to their customers through mobile-first, conversational research. We design immersive, in-the-moment research programs, pair them with smart data science and dynamic storytelling, and turn insight into action.

As part of Rival Group — alongside Rival Technologies and Angus Reid — we're helping transform the insights industry through AI-accelerated, messaging-based conversational insights. Our work reaches consumers and business audiences in ways that feel fresh, human, and genuinely useful.

We work with ambitious teams and global brands, and we take the work seriously without taking ourselves too seriously. You'll find a team that values trust, curiosity, ownership, creativity, and having a good time while doing meaningful work.

What you'll own


Produce accurate, well-formatted cross-tabulations from survey data using WinCross, SPSS, Microsoft Excel, and other relevant tools; review questionnaires and tabulation plans, clarify requirements, and deliver accurate outputs.
Complete rigorous quality checks on survey data and tables, investigate discrepancies, collaborate to resolve issues, and advise researchers on how to structure and interpret analysis outputs across different survey methods and designs.
Plan and prioritize work in ClickUp, track output, and improve turnaround time, accuracy, and productivity by testing AI and emerging tools, recommending process improvements, supporting new tool rollouts, and maintaining training and process documentation.


What you bring


At least 2 years of professional experience preparing, transforming, and tabulating market research survey data, plus a university or college degree or graduate certificate in market research, analytics, statistics, economics, social sciences, or another field involving research methods and data analysis.
Hands-on proficiency with SPSS and WinCross, strong Microsoft Excel skills, and experience working with survey datasets and producing cross-tabulations.
Clear, concise written and verbal communication skills, with a collaborative approach when working with local and remote teammates and research stakeholders.
A proactive, curious approach to change and ambiguity, with the judgment to test new ideas responsibly, evaluate their impact, and continuously improve data analysis workflows.
The ability to prioritize high-impact work, manage competing deadlines, stay organized, and consistently deliver accurate, high-quality outputs in a fast-moving environment.
Accountability for goals and deliverables, with the ability to work independently, collaborate effectively as part of a team, and bring a positive, solutions-oriented mindset as priorities evolve.


Nice to have


Familiarity with questionnaires, table specifications, banners, filters, and weighting is an asset.
Experience working in market research or public opinion research is preferred.


Why Reach3 for your next career adventure?

At Reach3, how we work matters just as much as what we deliver. We're building a place where people can do meaningful work, grow their careers, partner with great clients, and enjoy the humans they work with along the way.

Fair compensation: We're committed to pay equity and fair pay practices. The salary range for this role is $65,000 to $85,000, with final compensation based on skills, experience, and internal equity.


Home office, internet, and cellphone stipends
Retirement savings with employer matching
Parental leave top-up


Flexibility and time off: Flexible ways of working, home office support, and comprehensive paid time off so you can recharge and do your best work.


Hybrid or remote working model, depending on role and location
Comprehensive paid time off
Volunteer and professional development days


Health and wellness: Benefits that support the whole human, not just the employee.


Competitive health, vision, and dental benefits
Health spending account
Generous sick, personal, and mental health days
Additional health benefits with Canada Life


Our values

Our values guide how we work together, make decisions, and show up for customers and each other:


Courage
Results
Energy
Kinship


The not-so-fine print

You must be eligible to work in Canada to be considered for this role. At Reach3, we value the unique qualities and experiences each candidate brings. We personally review every application and do not use AI or automated systems to screen or filter resumes.

If you don't see yourself fully reflected in every requirement above, we still encourage you to apply. Research shows that people from underrepresented groups often apply only when they feel 100% qualified. We're proud to be an equal opportunity workplace committed to building a team culture that celebrates diversity, inclusion, and belonging.

Reach3 provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, religion, age, ancestry, gender, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, veteran status, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

We're also committed to an accessible work environment and inclusive employment practices. If you require accommodation at any point in the selection process, please email peopleteam@rivalgroup.io.

Please note that, given our security and compliance certifications, final applicants may be required to undergo a background check. No recruiters and no phone calls, please.

Title: Senior Business Data Analyst - Microsoft Fabric/One Lake
Description:
The ideal candidate has a blend of experience in both Management Consulting and Business Intelligence/ Analytics/Data Science to be able to work with clients to identify and frame their business problems, gather requirements, document use cases and functional design.




Data Analyst Skills include:




A Business Data Analyst (BA) at Capgemini will focus on the analysis, design and development of functional solutions for clients in a team environment. He/she will work alongside functional and industry specialists to assist with the creation of functional deliverables using established processes and procedures. He/she will contribute to client satisfaction by providing timely and responsive value-added services and work products and use individual functional knowledge to ensure work products and deliverables are of the highest caliber to ensure client satisfaction. Work will be performed under direct supervision to complete assigned tasks using already established procedures and best practices.




Business Analyst Is Responsible For:

• Drive content development for deliverable presentation(s)

• Gather business requirements with business.

• Define use cases with business & IT

• Articulate business outcomes and support value realization

• Facilitate and coordinate workshops with business & IT

• Data aggregation and analysis; ability to synthesize large quantities of information; translate data into meaningful insights and recommendations

• Solve clients' problems critically, structure analyses, construct analytical frameworks, and conceptualize storyboard/strategy development

• Lead workstream(s) independently and offer guidance to Data Engineers / Developers




Technical Experience Requirement

Experience working with Microsoft Fabric, OneLake, Power BI, Azure Data Services, or comparable cloud-based data platforms.

Knowledge of data governance, data quality, metadata management, and master data management principles.

Experience supporting Agile and SAFe delivery frameworks.

Strong stakeholder management, facilitation, and communication skills.

Experience creating process flows, business requirement documents (BRDs), functional requirement documents (FRDs), user stories, and use cases.

Title: Data Analyst, BC Children's Hospital Research
Description:
Data Analyst

BC Children's Hospital Research

Vancouver, BC

In accordance with the Mission, Vision and Values, and strategic directions of Provincial Health Services Authority patient safety is a priority and a responsibility shared by everyone at PHSA, and as such, the requirement to continuously improve quality and safety is inherent in all aspects of this position.

Reporting to Director, Quality Improvement and Evaluation, the Data Analyst is responsible for coordinating CHBC data requests, performing data extraction and complex data transformations, preparing information reports and collaborative analyses, performing data quality checking and documentation from various provincial datasets. This includes regular data quality monitoring, preparing data for analysis, and generating reports for the Provincial Health Services Authority (PHSA), the Ministry of Health (MoH), and care providers in the Health Authorities within British Columbia. This position supports monitoring of CHBC initiatives and provincial child health service performance indicators for use in the planning, implementation and evaluation of child and youth health care in the province. This position provides support to the CHBC Executive Director, and CHBC Leads and team members in performing management of data, analysis and reports. The Data Analyst advises others within the organization of the potential impacts of the specific data requirements of Data Sharing Agreements (DSA) and Information Sharing Plans (ISP) being executed and anticipates questions in order to problem solve in the process of due diligence.

What You’ll Do


Support for internal and external child and youth data needs to support evidence-based decision making, systems planning and policy-making as well as evaluation and research purposes by performing duties including: review of data availability, data extraction, data quality checking and cleaning, data manipulation and merging, and information summaries.
Develop complex data extraction and transformation scripts, including data linkages, to prepare data for analysis. Perform analysis and prepare reports and other analytical products (e.g. dashboards, scorecards). Implement indicators for monitoring and regular reporting.
Assist CHBC leadership team in the development of DSAs and ISPs to ensure the security of shared records and patient privacy.
Prepare a variety of materials including: confidential reports and correspondence, agreements, project outlines, meeting minutes and agendas with guidance Director of Quality Improvement, Evaluation and Projects to develop the Information Sharing Plan (ISP) and communicates with MoH or other data sources for data linkage. Link data sources from PHSA databases with other major health information systems such as the MoH hospital discharge database, Pharmanet, Medical Services Plan, and Vital Statistics. Take measures to protect all data and information sources to comply with protection of confidentiality and privacy policies.
Produce regular and ad hoc reports that monitor and benchmark cost, utilization and other quality and performance indicators for selected child services in BC and communicate findings to PHSA staff and external stakeholders at the local, regional, provincial and national levels.
Assist the development of a data quality and change management plan and related strategies to identify and implement prospective and concurrent methods to avoid, reduce and rectify data quality issues.
Provide support for the development and maintenance of data collection and recording systems such as databases, spreadsheets and web sites, including the design of standard and ad hoc reports. Write computer code and data queries to extract, capture and edit data.
Identify learning needs that contribute to skill enhancement and career progression for self and foster a working environment that stimulate learning and inquiry for the team. Take responsibility for keeping up-to-date on new initiatives, developments and trends in child health information sciences. Communicate information and make recommendations to the Director, Quality Improvement and Evaluation for evaluation and approval.


Qualifications

What you bring


A level of education, training, and experience equivalent to a Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Biostatistics or Health Informatics and one to three years of experience in health care organizations.
Demonstrated knowledge of the historic and ongoing impacts of settler colonialism on Indigenous Peoples in social and health contexts, including supported by significant knowledge of Indigenous-specific mandates, including clear understanding of and commitment to eradicate Indigenous-specific racism and discrimination and embed Indigenous Cultural Safety and Humility.
Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of the historic and ongoing impacts of settler colonialism and systemic racism on Indigenous Peoples within social and health contexts. This includes understanding how these factors contribute to current health disparities and barriers to care. Show a clear commitment to identifying, challenging, and eradicating Indigenous-specific racism and all forms of discrimination impacting equity-deserving groups within health care settings. This involves familiarity and understanding Indigenous Cultural Safety and Humility recognizing personal biases, institutional barriers, engaging in anti-racism education and training and advocating for systemic change.
Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of legislative obligations and provincial commitments within BC Children's Hospital Research contexts found in the foundational documents including Truth & Reconciliation Commission’s Calls to Action (2015), In Plain Sight (2020), BC's Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (2019), United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), Reclaiming Power and Place Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women & Girls Calls for Justice (2019), the Declaration Act Action Plan and Remembering Keegan: A First Nations Case Study - BC Human Rights Code, BC Anti-racism Act and how they intersect across the health care system.


Core Competencies


Brings an understanding of the Indigenous specific racism and the broader systemic racism that exists in the colonial health care structure, and has demonstrated initiatives in breaking down barriers and ensuring a safe environment ensuring a sense of belonging to all and informed by Indigenous Cultural Safety.
Awareness of social, economic, political and historical realities of settler colonialism on Indigenous Peoples and familiarity with addressing Indigenous-specific anti-racism, anti-racism and Indigenous Cultural Safety and foundational documents and legislative commitments (the Declaration Act, the Declaration Action Plan, TRC, IPS, Remembering Keegan, etc.).


Skills & Knowledge


Demonstrated ability to perform database querying, advanced data manipulation, analysis and information presentation through using relational database and statistical software. Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing. Demonstrated ability to use Microsoft operating systems, Excel, Access, Word. Demonstrated ability to use statistical software, such as SAS or R. Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills including the ability to comprehend complex issues, related data/information, and present information in concise meaningful ways. Demonstrated organization skills to generate work plans to handle multiple concurrent tasks, meet project deadlines within timeline, scope and budget. Physical ability to perform the duties of the job. Ability to understand and interpret data management concepts and processes and communicate complex ideas in simple terminology. Ability to develop complex and customized queries and reports. Ability to collaborate and work within a team while working independently.
Demonstrates a commitment to beginning and/or continuing their personal learning journey related to Indigenous-specific racism and dismantling systems of oppression, as well as addressing racism more broadly. Shows willingness to articulate and share their learning experiences to contribute to a culture of motivation and inspiration among peers.
Demonstrates foundational knowledge of the social, economic, and political realities of settler-colonialism and its impacts on Indigenous peoples and equity-deserving groups within social and health contexts. Understands the impact of social determinants of health-on-health outcomes. Shows a commitment to learning about and upholding legislative obligations and provincial commitments outlined in foundational documents such as the Truth & Reconciliation Commission’s Calls to Action (2015), In Plain Sight (2020), BC's Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (2019), United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), Reclaiming Power and Place: Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women & Girls Calls for Justice (2019), the Declaration Act Action Plan, Remembering Keegan: A First Nations Case Study, the BC Human Rights Code, Anti-Racism Data Act, and the Distinctions Based Approach.

Every PHSA employee enables the best possible patient care for our patients and their families. That’s why we’re focused on your care too – offering health, wellness, development programs to support you – at work and at home.

You will own the end-to-end analytics process for all experiments across product experiences—spanning measurement, data collection, experimentation, and insight generation.

Hands-On Analysis & Technical Execution

Evolve the experimentation analytics/data strategy across product

5+ years of experience in product analytics, data analytics, data science, business intelligence, or related fields

Strong expertise in business intelligence, dashboarding, and data visualization tools (Tableau, Power BI, Looker, etc.)
Strong experience with experimentation tools such as VWO
Deep understanding of product analytics and user behaviour metrics
Experience working in a cloud-based data warehouse environment (Azure, Snowflake, BigQuery, etc.)
Strong Experience with experimentation frameworks and A/B testing methodologies
Sets the standard for analytical rigour and excellence across the organisation

Title: Data Analyst, In-line Inspection
Description:
Your Job

We are seeking a Data Analyst for our Pipeline Inline Inspection (ILI) Data Analysis team.




DarkVision uses state-of-the-art proprietary acoustic imaging technologies to provide asset inspection services to industrial clients. Description:
Accelerate your success at Colliers.

Why Colliers?

As one of Canada’s leading commercial real estate services firms, we are driven by our mission to accelerate success for our people, clients, and communities.

A career at Colliers gives you the opportunity to make an impact, advance your career, and collaborate with top-tier talent. Don’t just take our word for it – we’ve been recognized as a top employer on a number of prestigious lists, including Best Workplaces in Canada, Best Workplaces for Women, Best Workplaces with Most Trusted Executive Teams, among others.

Toronto, ON / Vancouver, BC; Hybrid

About The Role

The Portfolio Intelligence Analyst is responsible for producing trusted portfolio intelligence that enables effective enterprise portfolio management and informed executive decision-making. Reporting to the Enterprise Portfolio Manager, the role gathers, validates, analyses and maintains portfolio information across the enterprise technology portfolio. The Portfolio Intelligence Analyst develops executive dashboards, portfolio analytics, governance information and performance reporting while supporting portfolio planning, investment prioritization, and ongoing portfolio monitoring.

The role ensures portfolio information is complete, accurate, timely, and decision-ready, providing the analytical foundation upon which portfolio governance, investment decisions and executive reporting are based.

In this role, you will…

Portfolio Analysis and Intelligence


Analyze portfolio data to support prioritization, investment planning, capacity management, financial oversight, dependency management, and portfolio health assessments.
Develop actionable insights, identify trends, risks, and data anomalies, and provide recommendations to support strategic decision-making.


Executive Reporting and Governance Support


Develop and maintain executive dashboards, scorecards, portfolio reports, governance packs, and performance metrics.
Support governance forums by preparing briefing materials, decision-support information, meeting documentation, and tracking governance actions and outcomes.
Ensure reporting is timely, accurate, consistent, and tailored for executive audiences.


Business Case and Investment Support


Support business case intake, validation, investment appraisal, and enterprise portfolio prioritization activities.
Maintain business case repositories and associated supporting documentation.


Portfolio Health Monitoring & Continuous Improvement


Monitor portfolio financial performance, resource utilization, delivery health, risks, dependencies, benefits realization, and key portfolio metrics.
Maintain high standards of data quality and information integrity across the portfolio.
Identify and implement improvements to portfolio analytics, reporting, processes, automation, and AI-enabled portfolio intelligence capabilities.


What You Bring


Basic / Minimum Education requirement to perform the job: Bachelor's degree
Preferred educational requirements to perform the job:
Certified Business Analysis Professional (CBAP)
SAFe® Lean Portfolio Management (LPM)
SAFe® Product Owner/Product Manager (POPM)
Kanban Management Professional (KMP)
Management of Portfolios (MoP®)
PRINCE2® Foundation
Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate (PL-300)
Relevant Years of experience required to perform the role: 3 to 5 yrs of experience
Experience working within project, program, or Agile frameworks is an asset and preferred
Commercial Real Estate experience / background to perform the role is preferred

Pursuant to local law, Colliers is disclosing the following information:

Area/Location Specific: Toronto, ON & Vancouver, BC

Data Analyst

Vancouver, BC

In accordance with the Mission, Vision and Values, and strategic directions of Provincial Health Services Authority patient safety is a priority and a responsibility shared by everyone at PHSA, and as such, the requirement to continuously improve quality and safety is inherent in all aspects of this position.

Reporting to Director, Quality Improvement and Evaluation, the Data Analyst is responsible for coordinating CHBC data requests, performing data extraction and complex data transformations, preparing information reports and collaborative analyses, performing data quality checking and documentation from various provincial datasets. This includes regular data quality monitoring, preparing data for analysis, and generating reports for the Provincial Health Services Authority (PHSA), the Ministry of Health (MoH), and care providers in the Health Authorities within British Columbia. This position supports monitoring of CHBC initiatives and provincial child health service performance indicators for use in the planning, implementation and evaluation of child and youth health care in the province. This position provides support to the CHBC Executive Director, and CHBC Leads and team members in performing management of data, analysis and reports. The Data Analyst advises others within the organization of the potential impacts of the specific data requirements of Data Sharing Agreements (DSA) and Information Sharing Plans (ISP) being executed and anticipates questions in order to problem solve in the process of due diligence.

What You’ll Do


Support for internal and external child and youth data needs to support evidence-based decision making, systems planning and policy-making as well as evaluation and research purposes by performing duties including: review of data availability, data extraction, data quality checking and cleaning, data manipulation and merging, and information summaries.
Develop complex data extraction and transformation scripts, including data linkages, to prepare data for analysis. Perform analysis and prepare reports and other analytical products (e.g. dashboards, scorecards). Implement indicators for monitoring and regular reporting.
Assist CHBC leadership team in the development of DSAs and ISPs to ensure the security of shared records and patient privacy.
Prepare a variety of materials including: confidential reports and correspondence, agreements, project outlines, meeting minutes and agendas with guidance Director of Quality Improvement, Evaluation and Projects to develop the Information Sharing Plan (ISP) and communicates with MoH or other data sources for data linkage. Link data sources from PHSA databases with other major health information systems such as the MoH hospital discharge database, Pharmanet, Medical Services Plan, and Vital Statistics. Take measures to protect all data and information sources to comply with protection of confidentiality and privacy policies.
Produce regular and ad hoc reports that monitor and benchmark cost, utilization and other quality and performance indicators for selected child services in BC and communicate findings to PHSA staff and external stakeholders at the local, regional, provincial and national levels.
Assist the development of a data quality and change management plan and related strategies to identify and implement prospective and concurrent methods to avoid, reduce and rectify data quality issues.
Provide support for the development and maintenance of data collection and recording systems such as databases, spreadsheets and web sites, including the design of standard and ad hoc reports. Write computer code and data queries to extract, capture and edit data.
Identify learning needs that contribute to skill enhancement and career progression for self and foster a working environment that stimulate learning and inquiry for the team. Take responsibility for keeping up-to-date on new initiatives, developments and trends in child health information sciences. Communicate information and make recommendations to the Director, Quality Improvement and Evaluation for evaluation and approval.


Qualifications

What you bring


A level of education, training, and experience equivalent to a Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Biostatistics or Health Informatics and one to three years of experience in health care organizations.
Demonstrated knowledge of the historic and ongoing impacts of settler colonialism on Indigenous Peoples in social and health contexts, including supported by significant knowledge of Indigenous-specific mandates, including clear understanding of and commitment to eradicate Indigenous-specific racism and discrimination and embed Indigenous Cultural Safety and Humility.
Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of the historic and ongoing impacts of settler colonialism and systemic racism on Indigenous Peoples within social and health contexts. This includes understanding how these factors contribute to current health disparities and barriers to care. Show a clear commitment to identifying, challenging, and eradicating Indigenous-specific racism and all forms of discrimination impacting equity-deserving groups within health care settings. This involves familiarity and understanding Indigenous Cultural Safety and Humility recognizing personal biases, institutional barriers, engaging in anti-racism education and training and advocating for systemic change.
Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of legislative obligations and provincial commitments within BC Children's Hospital Research contexts found in the foundational documents including Truth & Reconciliation Commission’s Calls to Action (2015), In Plain Sight (2020), BC's Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (2019), United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), Reclaiming Power and Place Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women & Girls Calls for Justice (2019), the Declaration Act Action Plan and Remembering Keegan: A First Nations Case Study - BC Human Rights Code, BC Anti-racism Act and how they intersect across the health care system.


Core Competencies


Brings an understanding of the Indigenous specific racism and the broader systemic racism that exists in the colonial health care structure, and has demonstrated initiatives in breaking down barriers and ensuring a safe environment ensuring a sense of belonging to all and informed by Indigenous Cultural Safety.
Awareness of social, economic, political and historical realities of settler colonialism on Indigenous Peoples and familiarity with addressing Indigenous-specific anti-racism, anti-racism and Indigenous Cultural Safety and foundational documents and legislative commitments (the Declaration Act, the Declaration Action Plan, TRC, IPS, Remembering Keegan, etc.).


Skills & Knowledge


Demonstrated ability to perform database querying, advanced data manipulation, analysis and information presentation through using relational database and statistical software. Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing. Demonstrated ability to use Microsoft operating systems, Excel, Access, Word. Demonstrated ability to use statistical software, such as SAS or R. Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills including the ability to comprehend complex issues, related data/information, and present information in concise meaningful ways. Demonstrated organization skills to generate work plans to handle multiple concurrent tasks, meet project deadlines within timeline, scope and budget. Physical ability to perform the duties of the job. Ability to understand and interpret data management concepts and processes and communicate complex ideas in simple terminology. Ability to develop complex and customized queries and reports. Ability to collaborate and work within a team while working independently.
Demonstrates a commitment to beginning and/or continuing their personal learning journey related to Indigenous-specific racism and dismantling systems of oppression, as well as addressing racism more broadly. Shows willingness to articulate and share their learning experiences to contribute to a culture of motivation and inspiration among peers.
Demonstrates foundational knowledge of the social, economic, and political realities of settler-colonialism and its impacts on Indigenous peoples and equity-deserving groups within social and health contexts. Understands the impact of social determinants of health-on-health outcomes. Shows a commitment to learning about and upholding legislative obligations and provincial commitments outlined in foundational documents such as the Truth & Reconciliation Commission’s Calls to Action (2015), In Plain Sight (2020), BC's Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (2019), United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), Reclaiming Power and Place: Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women & Girls Calls for Justice (2019), the Declaration Act Action Plan, Remembering Keegan: A First Nations Case Study, the BC Human Rights Code, Anti-Racism Data Act, and the Distinctions Based Approach.

Every PHSA employee enables the best possible patient care for our patients and their families. Whether you are providing direct care, conducting research, or making it possible for others to do their work, you impact the lives of British Columbians today and in the future. That’s why we’re focused on your care too – offering health, wellness, development programs to support you – at work and at home.

Data Analyst

BC Children's Hospital Research

Vancouver, BC

In accordance with the Mission, Vision and Values, and strategic directions of Provincial Health Services Authority patient safety is a priority and a responsibility shared by everyone at PHSA, and as such, the requirement to continuously improve quality and safety is inherent in all aspects of this position.

Reporting to Director, Quality Improvement and Evaluation, the Data Analyst is responsible for coordinating CHBC data requests, performing data extraction and complex data transformations, preparing information reports and collaborative analyses, performing data quality checking and documentation from various provincial datasets. This includes regular data quality monitoring, preparing data for analysis, and generating reports for the Provincial Health Services Authority (PHSA), the Ministry of Health (MoH), and care providers in the Health Authorities within British Columbia. This position supports monitoring of CHBC initiatives and provincial child health service performance indicators for use in the planning, implementation and evaluation of child and youth health care in the province. This position provides support to the CHBC Executive Director, and CHBC Leads and team members in performing management of data, analysis and reports. The Data Analyst advises others within the organization of the potential impacts of the specific data requirements of Data Sharing Agreements (DSA) and Information Sharing Plans (ISP) being executed and anticipates questions in order to problem solve in the process of due diligence.

What You’ll Do

  • Support for internal and external child and youth data needs to support evidence-based decision making, systems planning and policy-making as well as evaluation and research purposes by performing duties including: review of data availability, data extraction, data quality checking and cleaning, data manipulation and merging, and information summaries.
  • Develop complex data extraction and transformation scripts, including data linkages, to prepare data for analysis. Perform analysis and prepare reports and other analytical products (e.g. dashboards, scorecards). Implement indicators for monitoring and regular reporting.
  • Assist CHBC leadership team in the development of DSAs and ISPs to ensure the security of shared records and patient privacy.
  • Prepare a variety of materials including: confidential reports and correspondence, agreements, project outlines, meeting minutes and agendas with guidance Director of Quality Improvement, Evaluation and Projects to develop the Information Sharing Plan (ISP) and communicates with MoH or other data sources for data linkage. Link data sources from PHSA databases with other major health information systems such as the MoH hospital discharge database, Pharmanet, Medical Services Plan, and Vital Statistics. Take measures to protect all data and information sources to comply with protection of confidentiality and privacy policies.
  • Produce regular and ad hoc reports that monitor and benchmark cost, utilization and other quality and performance indicators for selected child services in BC and communicate findings to PHSA staff and external stakeholders at the local, regional, provincial and national levels.
  • Assist the development of a data quality and change management plan and related strategies to identify and implement prospective and concurrent methods to avoid, reduce and rectify data quality issues.
  • Provide support for the development and maintenance of data collection and recording systems such as databases, spreadsheets and web sites, including the design of standard and ad hoc reports. Write computer code and data queries to extract, capture and edit data.
  • Identify learning needs that contribute to skill enhancement and career progression for self and foster a working environment that stimulate learning and inquiry for the team. Take responsibility for keeping up-to-date on new initiatives, developments and trends in child health information sciences. Communicate information and make recommendations to the Director, Quality Improvement and Evaluation for evaluation and approval.

Qualifications

What you bring

  • A level of education, training, and experience equivalent to a Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Biostatistics or Health Informatics and one to three years of experience in health care organizations.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of the historic and ongoing impacts of settler colonialism on Indigenous Peoples in social and health contexts, including supported by significant knowledge of Indigenous-specific mandates, including clear understanding of and commitment to eradicate Indigenous-specific racism and discrimination and embed Indigenous Cultural Safety and Humility.
  • Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of the historic and ongoing impacts of settler colonialism and systemic racism on Indigenous Peoples within social and health contexts. This includes understanding how these factors contribute to current health disparities and barriers to care. Show a clear commitment to identifying, challenging, and eradicating Indigenous-specific racism and all forms of discrimination impacting equity-deserving groups within health care settings. This involves familiarity and understanding Indigenous Cultural Safety and Humility recognizing personal biases, institutional barriers, engaging in anti-racism education and training and advocating for systemic change.
  • Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of legislative obligations and provincial commitments within BC Children's Hospital Research contexts found in the foundational documents including Truth & Reconciliation Commission’s Calls to Action (2015), In Plain Sight (2020), BC's Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (2019), United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), Reclaiming Power and Place Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women & Girls Calls for Justice (2019), the Declaration Act Action Plan and Remembering Keegan: A First Nations Case Study - BC Human Rights Code, BC Anti-racism Act and how they intersect across the health care system.

Core Competencies

  • Brings an understanding of the Indigenous specific racism and the broader systemic racism that exists in the colonial health care structure, and has demonstrated initiatives in breaking down barriers and ensuring a safe environment ensuring a sense of belonging to all and informed by Indigenous Cultural Safety.
  • Awareness of social, economic, political and historical realities of settler colonialism on Indigenous Peoples and familiarity with addressing Indigenous-specific anti-racism, anti-racism and Indigenous Cultural Safety and foundational documents and legislative commitments (the Declaration Act, the Declaration Action Plan, TRC, IPS, Remembering Keegan, etc.).

Skills & Knowledge

  • Demonstrated ability to perform database querying, advanced data manipulation, analysis and information presentation through using relational database and statistical software. Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing. Demonstrated ability to use Microsoft operating systems, Excel, Access, Word. Demonstrated ability to use statistical software, such as SAS or R. Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills including the ability to comprehend complex issues, related data/information, and present information in concise meaningful ways. Demonstrated organization skills to generate work plans to handle multiple concurrent tasks, meet project deadlines within timeline, scope and budget. Physical ability to perform the duties of the job. Ability to understand and interpret data management concepts and processes and communicate complex ideas in simple terminology. Ability to develop complex and customized queries and reports. Ability to collaborate and work within a team while working independently.
  • Demonstrates a commitment to beginning and/or continuing their personal learning journey related to Indigenous-specific racism and dismantling systems of oppression, as well as addressing racism more broadly. Shows willingness to articulate and share their learning experiences to contribute to a culture of motivation and inspiration among peers.
  • Demonstrates foundational knowledge of the social, economic, and political realities of settler-colonialism and its impacts on Indigenous peoples and equity-deserving groups within social and health contexts. Understands the impact of social determinants of health-on-health outcomes. Shows a commitment to learning about and upholding legislative obligations and provincial commitments outlined in foundational documents such as the Truth & Reconciliation Commission’s Calls to Action (2015), In Plain Sight (2020), BC's Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (2019), United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), Reclaiming Power and Place: Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women & Girls Calls for Justice (2019), the Declaration Act Action Plan, Remembering Keegan: A First Nations Case Study, the BC Human Rights Code, Anti-Racism Data Act, and the Distinctions Based Approach.

What We Bring

Every PHSA employee enables the best possible patient care for our patients and their families. Whether you are providing direct care, conducting research, or making it possible for others to do their work, you impact the lives of British Columbians today and in the future. That’s why we’re focused on your care too – offering health, wellness, development programs to support you – at work and at home.

  • Join one of BC’s largest employers with province-wide programs, services and operations – offering vast opportunities for growth, development, and recognition programs that honour the commitment and contribution of all employees.
  • Access to professional development opportunities through our in-house training programs, including +2,000 courses, such as our San’yas Indigenous Cultural Safety Training course, or Core Linx for Leadership roles.
  • Enjoy a comprehensive benefits package, including municipal pension plan, and psychological health & safety programs and holistic wellness resources.
  • Annual statutory holidays (13) with generous vacation entitlement and accruement.
  • PHSA is a remote work friendly employer, welcoming flexible work options to support our people (eligibility may vary, depending on position).
  • Access to WorkPerks, a premium discount program offering a wide range of local and national discounts on electronics, entertainment, dining, travel, wellness, apparel, and more.
